F1_mechanism.disclosure: check_canonical_numerator=true compares canonical numerators first. When that comparison fails and samples > 0 (default 5), it falls back to the sampled certificate, so every sampled-path change (the 36c1 normalizer and the e3f9 nonfinite guard) also changes canonical-mode results. With default samples, DIS19 canonical goes from 76 to 74 through this fallback. Pure canonical (samples 0) is unchanged on DIS19: 76 at both A and e3f9, with identical partitions. 36c1 also adds the normalizer and a finite-ratio check to the exact path in compare_atoms, but no outcome change was observed there; the CI pure-canonical rows pass at both.
